correctness.rationale: Write K=3-M_0. The product of means uses binomial marginal probabilities; the joint term sums only distinct boxes, with the unused mass (1-p_i-p_j)^{n-r}. At r=n a zero mass to the zero power means there are no remaining allocations, so the factor is one. The common binomial and denominator factors are positive, leaving the sign of H. Independent ordered-allocation dynamic programming produced all fourteen signs ++++-+++++---- at n=14. Separate integer maximization of the positive and negative bases reproduced the four displayed pairs and checked that the certified ratios to the powers t,2t,2t,t exceed the appropriate opposing term counts 6 or 9 already at t=15. Since all ratios exceed one, this proves the signs for every later integer t. The strict inequalities persist simultaneously by continuity after normalization of the positive weights (the max of finitely many continuous bases is continuous), preserving the same lower bounds and hence the same cutoff uniformly. Two boxes have M_0 M_r=0 for r<n and positive means of M_0 and M_r; M_n=M_0 gives strict negative covariance at n for n>=2 and positive box probabilities. One box has constant K. The infinite claim is at least three sign reversals witnessed by the sampled signs (sign variation ignoring zeros), not an exact sign sequence or a claim of exactly three switches for all large n.
